title: A little x64 interpreter
description:
Run a short list of x64-style instructions on simulated registers, flags and a stack.

```
mov ecx, 5
xor eax, eax
loop: add eax, ecx
dec ecx
jnz loop
ret
-> eax = 15, 18 instructions run
```
hints: `<sstream>` gives streams over strings. `std::istringstream in{ text };` reads from a string exactly like `std::cin` (`in >> word >> number`, or `std::getline(in, line)` for one line at a time), and its condition is false once a read fails. `std::ostringstream out; out << "x " << 5; out.str()` builds a string the way `std::cout` prints.
First pass: find labels and their line numbers. Second pass: run with an instruction pointer that is a line index (lesson 7.07).
Parse each line into an opcode and up to two operands; an operand is a register name or a number.
requirements: Registers rax to rdi (64-bit), ZF and SF, a stack, and labels.
Instructions: `mov`, `add`, `sub`, `xor`, `inc`, `dec`, `cmp`, `jmp`, `jz`, `jnz`, `push`, `pop`, `ret` (ret with an empty stack ends the program).
Writing a 32-bit register (like `eax`) clears the top half, as real x64 does.
Report an unknown instruction with its line number.
